evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, apparatus combinations, values and planned figures are original. P2 provides demand patterns only. No P1 lesson assignment inferred.

questions.prompt: State what is meant by coherent waves and give one reason why coherence matters in a two-source interference experiment.
Two in-phase sources produce waves of wavelength 5.0 cm. At point P, the two path lengths differ by 7.5 cm. What occurs at P if the wave amplitudes there are equal?
Which arrangement is most likely to produce a stable sound interference pattern?

options.A: Two unrelated loudspeakers playing nearly equal notes
options.B: One signal generator feeding two loudspeakers of similar output
options.C: One loudspeaker and one silent microphone
options.D: Two loudspeakers separated so their waves never overlap

questions.prompt: A two-source pattern has maxima but its minima remain fairly strong. Which change is most likely to make the contrast clearer?

options.A: Make the wave amplitudes at the observation region more nearly equal
options.B: Allow the relative phase to drift
options.D: Use a detector that averages over several maxima and minima

questions.prompt: A student demonstrates two-source interference of sound.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe an arrangement that produces and detects a stable pattern of maxima and minima.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why using two independent signal generators could make the observed pattern unstable.

questions.prompt: Monochromatic light illuminates two narrow slits. A screen is placed beyond the slits.

figure.purpose: Assess qualitative two-slit source and observation conditions without introducing fringe-spacing calculation.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a monochromatic source illuminating two narrow slits and a blank screen. Show no fringes, distances, answers or formula.
figure.alt_text: A monochromatic source illuminates two narrow slits with a screen beyond.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain why the two slits can act as coherent sources.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State two other conditions or design choices needed for clear observable fringes.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State what is observed on the screen.

questions.prompt: Two in-phase microwave transmitters X and Y are supplied by one oscillator. At detector P, XP = 1.26 m and YP = 1.44 m. The wavelength is 0.12 m. Each transmitter directs microwaves through an opening before they enter the observation region.

figure.purpose: Provide the apparatus geometry and labelled routes needed for the path-difference calculation.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white spatial diagram with transmitters X and Y, one opening in front of each, detector P and straight construction lines labelled XP = 1.26 m and YP = 1.44 m. Do not draw wavefronts, ray spreading, an overlap region, working or any interference classification.
figure.alt_text: Two microwave transmitters, two openings and detector P with paths XP of 1.26 m and YP of 1.44 m.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the path difference at P in wavelengths.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State and explain whether P is at an intensity maximum or minimum.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain how diffraction at the openings helps an interference pattern to be observed across a region containing P.
